chunks: And by his chain, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub Al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who arranged (the emancipation of) an owned slave of his. Then he became needy to his price. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'He is his slave; if he so desires, he sells him, and if he so desires, he emancipates him, and if he so desires, he keeps him until he dies. So when the master dies, he is free, from his third (of the deceased's estate).'

key_terms.ثُلُثِهِ: His third (referring to the portion of estate for bequests)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a master who needs money after arranging his slave's emancipation?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies that a 'mudabbir' remains the master's property until death, allowing the master to liquidate the slave's value by selling or keeping the slave, with the cost deducted from the one-third estate portion reserved for bequests. This ruling highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding deferred emancipation, distinguishing it from immediate manumission and ensuring the financial obligation is settled from the testator's discretionary share rather than the fixed inheritance portions.

en.hubeali: And by his chain, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub Al Khazzaz, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,

‘I asked Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> about a man who arranged (the emancipation of) an owned slave of his. Then he became needy to his price. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He is his slave, if he so desires to he sells him, and if he so desires to he emancipates him, and if he so desire to he keeps him until he dies. So when the master dies, so he is free, from his third (of the deceased)’.
